findings.description: At 00:00 the bowl holds 8 balls (2 red, 3 yellow, 3 green). Between 00:00.25 and 00:00.75 the child's hand reaches into the bowl and lifts out a red ball, yet at 00:01.00 the bowl still shows the identical 8-ball arrangement including both red balls, with an extra red ball in the child's hands. No ball was brought in from outside the bowl; a red ball has effectively been duplicated.

Before stirring (00:04.75) the bowl holds 3 red, 3 yellow, 3 green balls. During hand-stirring, with no balls added or removed, the composition drifts: at 00:07.75 at least 4-5 distinct red balls are visible with only one yellow; at 00:09.25 there are ~4 red and ~4 green and no yellow; at 00:09.50 ~5 red, 1 yellow, 1 green. Yellow balls vanish and red balls multiply without any visible cause.

The balls are rigid glossy spheres in 00:00-00:05. From ~00:06 onward while stirred they render as lumpy, pinched, egg- or pepper-shaped blobs (e.g. the yellow at upper right at 00:06.00, the stretched red and green at 00:09.25) beyond what motion blur explains, implying a material/shape transformation with no cause.
